title.narrative: South Africa Joint Strategy on Just Energy Transition-SDGs

description.narrative: South Africa is forging ahead on the pathway towards an inclusive, just and sustainable socioeconomic transformation driven by equitable and affordable access to clean energy and low carbon job-intensive economy growth. This joint programme is envisaged to have four interlinked and well-coordinated components in line with the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework, as it relates to the Just Energy Transition in South Africa: i) leaving no one behind; ii) supporting the new energy mix; iii) ensuring the financing mix works for all; and iv) stakeholders’ engagement. The programme will work with key actors and strategic partners across the energy spectrum in South Africa to ensure that communities, entrepreneurs, workers particularly those linked to the coal value-chain as well as women, youth, SMMEs, rural workers, persons with disabilities, and refugees and asylum seekers are not only protected from the adverse impacts of the transition, but are an integral part of the greener, new and independent economy that will emerge as part of the transition. They will actively engage in the new emerging (e.g. new electric vehicles, battery storage systems) and transformed sectors (e.g. food systems) and will be essential in shaping these outcomes.
